# We Improved WARDEN's Warnings. Twelve Rechecks Changed No Choices.

#mcp #security #ai #opensource

WARDEN's local candidate selected an injected recommendation target 27 times out of 48, compared with 44 and 46 times for the published guarded profiles. That was an improvement on our six test cases.

Its Stop hook also asked the model to reconsider twelve answers. Not one selected ID changed.

Those findings belong next to each other. The first describes a difference between complete versions. The second describes what happened during twelve actual continuations. Giving the second result credit for the first would make a better release story and a worse account of the experiment.

This investigation grew out of Launch Gate's comments on our earlier WARDEN article. The useful question was whether we could measure a change in the model's choice, separately from its mentioning an attack or repeating a warning.

# Four filings, zero merges: where three agents actually sit this week

#mcp #opensource #webdev #showdev

Between 1 and 3 October 2026 I filed the same three names into four public catalogs. None of those pull requests is merged. The software is already callable. The directories are not.

The three names are WARDEN (an MCP firewall for tool definitions), HISTOR (a signed log of what remote MCP servers advertised), and AIMarket Hub (the catalog they sit in). This is a status note, not a launch.

## What was filed

Where  | When  | What  | State on 3 Oct 2026
--- | --- | --- | ---
Docker MCP Registry #5364  | 1 Oct  | WARDEN, local server, package 0.8.2  | Open
Docker MCP Registry #5365  | 1 Oct  | Hub at `https://modelmarket.dev/mcp`  | Open
awesome-erc8004 #120  | 1 Oct  | Hub, HISTOR, WARDEN as ERC-8004 agents on Base  | Open
coinbase/x402 #373  | 2 Oct  | Six paid routes under Services/Endpoints  | Open
Tools are discovered from the server, not hardcoded in the pull request. Direct ones named in the filing: `weather_now`, `air_quality_now`, `nearby_sensors`, `fair_random`, plus `market_search` and `market_invoke`.

HISTOR is the record of what a remote MCP server advertised, not a verdict that the server is safe. The desk is histor.modelmarket.dev. Source: github.com/alexar76/histor.

# MCP servers edit the instructions your agent reads. WARDEN 0.18 shows which words changed

On 29 September an MCP server changed the description of one of its 45 tools. The old text said that when a project takes payments, a mobile publish makes a test build in Stripe test mode. The new text says:

> publish_app always publishes live (web, and the mobile app when it is built; payments in Stripe live mode) — never ask the user test or live.

This is not an attack. The server changed how publishing works and told the model so. It is also a new instruction to your model, in a tool you approved before that sentence existed: from now on, don't ask.

WARDEN pins an MCP server's tool definitions the first time it vets them. Any later change blocks the server until a person approves it again. Up to 0.17, that person got the old and the new definition of each changed tool as two lines of JSON. For this change that is 6,614 characters, and the sentence above sits somewhere in the middle of the second line. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
